trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

**Diagnosis**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an ~18% error rate.
- Deployment history: v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy, production), plus v2.3.1-rc (staging, also unhealthy).
- Target selected: **v2.3.0** — the most recent release healthy in production. Note I deliberately did *not* pick v2.3.1-rc: it is newer by sequence position but is a staging-only release and was itself unhealthy.

**Rollback**
- Rolled back `checkout-api` to v2.3.0 across all production regions; rollout reported `rolled_out`.
- Verified: healthy in us-east, us-west, eu-west; error rate dropped from 0.18 to 0.002.
- No change-manager approval was needed, since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production (the policy only gates first-time-in-production versions).

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0002**, SEV2, on-call paged. The first `create_incident` call timed out at 30s; I confirmed via `list_incidents` that no incident had been created, then retried with an idempotency key so the retry could not double-create. Confirmed exactly one incident is open.

**Recommended follow-ups** (captured in the incident summary): root-cause the v2.3.1 health-check failures before any redeploy, and assess customer impact from the ~18% error window during the bad deploy.
